headline: Govt to ban road digging in Dhaka during monsoon
summary: The government has shifted the fiscal year to ensure all road repairs are completed during the dry season to reduce public suffering and traffic congestion.
details: The government has decided to ban all road digging and repair work in Dhaka during the monsoon season. To implement this, all road maintenance must be completed during the dry season, a rule that will take effect next year.
In a meeting chaired by Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed at the Secretariat, it was decided that police permission is now mandatory before any roadwork begins in the city.
To monitor progress and control traffic, a coordination meeting involving all relevant agencies will be held every 15 days, presided over by the Home Minister.

Contractors must now carry out work on weekdays from 10 PM to 6 AM and can work 24 hours on Fridays and Saturdays. They are also required to provide safety measures and notify the public through media before starting.
The government has also shifted the fiscal year from July 1-June 30 to April 1-March 31 specifically to ensure that construction work avoids the rainy season.
Additionally, the meeting addressed the control of battery-operated rickshaws, deciding to disconnect all illegal charging points using mobile courts during the day.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed emphasized that the goal is to reduce public suffering and prevent the waste of time and money caused by repeated digging of the same spots by different agencies.
caption:
No more road digging in Dhaka during the monsoon! The government is even changing the fiscal year to make it happen.

The government has decided to ban all road digging and repair work in Dhaka during the monsoon season. To implement this, all road maintenance must be completed during the dry season, a rule that will take effect next year.

In a meeting chaired by Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed at the Secretariat, it was decided that police permission is now mandatory before any roadwork begins in the city.

To monitor progress and control traffic, a coordination meeting involving all relevant agencies will be held every 15 days, presided over by the Home Minister.

Contractors must now carry out work on weekdays from 10 PM to 6 AM and can work 24 hours on Fridays and Saturdays. They are also required to provide safety measures and notify the public through media before starting.

The government has also shifted the fiscal year from July 1-June 30 to April 1-March 31 specifically to ensure that construction work avoids the rainy season.

Additionally, the meeting addressed the control of battery-operated rickshaws, deciding to disconnect all illegal charging points using mobile courts during the day.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed emphasized that the goal is to reduce public suffering and prevent the waste of time and money caused by repeated digging of the same spots by different agencies.
